Where it sits and what to know here

items.t: All twelve visible cards are labelled with the sub-area "Serpentine" and Surrey addresses on the city's southern lowland — 40 Avenue, 176 Street (Highway 15), 196 Street, 168 Street, 188 Street and 184 Street — spanning acreage houses, blueberry farms, vacant land and Campbell Heights industrial-side parcels, with listing text referencing Morgan Creek, Grandview Heights and the US border.
FVREB publishes no public street-level sub-area boundary.

Board figures (with the conflict carried, not resolved): Serpentine sub-area, September 2026 (inventory / sales / sales ratio) — Detached: 0 / 0 / NA; Condos & Townhomes: 0 / 0 / NA — a genuine zero-activity row in the published report, not a missing row. The rest of the set: Clayton Detached 34/10/29%, attached 96/20/21%; Cloverdale Detached 167/22/13%, attached 98/17/17% — and the three sub-area rows sum to the community totals in both splits. The board does not publish sub-area medians.

Depreciation reports and CRF (strata stock generally): since July 1, 2024, stratas with five or more lots must obtain a depreciation report every five years, no deferral by vote; and since November 1, 2023, stratas must contribute at least 10% of the operating fund to the CRF. Neither rule creates strata stock on this area.

A zero row is not a missing row. SnapStats publishes a Serpentine row — it simply records 0 / 0 / NA in both splits for September 2026, and the three sub-area rows still sum exactly to the Cloverdale community totals (Detached 34 + 167 + 0 = 201; attached 96 + 98 + 0 = 194), so the zero is internal to the published data, not a gap.

faq.a: Confirm which ground a specific listing sits on from its address, not from the sub-area label.
faq.q: Is Serpentine in Cloverdale or South Surrey?

faq.a: On the worked example in — inputs: $1,212,500 fair market value (the community detached median, illustration only), fully residential, no exemption — the bill is $22,250. Farm and mixed-use parcels can split portions; have a lawyer or notary model the exact bill.
faq.q: What PTT should I budget on this ground?

faq.a: Not while the parcel is in the ALR — ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s.6; Strata Property Act s.239), and subdivision itself needs ALC permission.
faq.q: Could a townhouse project be built on a Serpentine farm parcel?

faq.a: The monthly strata fee, amounts owing, approved special levies, the CRF balance, insurance, rules, budget and financial statement, any Rental Disclosure Statement, and the depreciation report attached — within seven days of request, fee capped at $35 plus up to 25 cents per page.
faq.q: What does the Form B tell me if my search leads me to a strata townhouse nearby?

faq.a: $16,000 with no exemption — 1% on the first $200,000 plus 2% on the remaining $700,000 (BC Government, PTT). Farm-class and other parcel-specific positions are a title-and-assessment check, not a page figure.
faq.q: How much property transfer tax would I pay on a $900,000 acreage purchase?

faq.a: Each one is checked on its own: ALR status on ALC mapping, zone and designation in the City's mapping, and servicing on documents, not listing text.
faq.q: Can I buy a vacant lot or farm parcel here?

faq.a: Confirm servicing with the City and on the ground, approvals against City records, and any court-ordered sale against court records; Surrey has no Supreme Court registry.
faq.q: Can I trust a card's "city water," "preload" or "court-ordered" wording?

faq.a: Verify servicing and water parcel by parcel (City records, GWELLS, Fraser Health) — on farm ground that answer drives value more than the house does.
faq.q: The card says city water / a well / services at lot line — can I rely on it?

faq.a: It is a board sub-area name only — not a City of Surrey planning name, with no City boundary.
